title: Apron Order
primary_metric: total job cost (material + marking labor) for a 40-apron batch

options.A: Cut on the Fold -- 1 1/4 yd/apron, 3 min/apron marking time
options.B: Cut Open -- 1 1/6 yards fabric, 6 min/apron marking time

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

deliverables.text: Waist tie length: 2/3 x body panel width.
Trimmed marker length: subtract two end-trims from a raw marker segment.
Aprons per bolt: bolt yardage divided by yardage-per-apron.
Splitting a remnant into 5 equal pieces.
How many seam allowances fit in the hem depth.
Total cost verdict: material + labor for both layouts.

balance.argument_a: 3 fewer minutes of marking time per apron, times 40 aprons, is 120 minutes -- 2 hours -- of labor saved, worth $32.00 at $16.00/hr.
balance.argument_b: Real fabric savings -- 1/12 yard less waste and less fabric per apron, adding up across forty aprons.
balance.margin_basis: Total job cost (yards x price + minutes x labor rate) for a 40-apron batch, computed in cases/apron-order/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix A/C/D figures.

derived._note: Computed by cases/apron-order/sensitivity_model.py, cost_breakdown(PARAMS). case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Grounded in real, general wage data for fabric-cutting production roles (mid-teens per hour); not independently verified against a single primary wage source (direct fetch attempts were blocked), so stated as an assumption rather than cited as sourced.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5: margin ranges 2.00%-13.64%, Option A stays cheaper throughout.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Yardage and marking-time figures per apron, per layout
modeling_assumptions.basis: Devon's own shop's real marker layout for this authored pattern; no public database of real garment-shop marker results exists for this specific pattern.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not swept in Tier 2 probe 5 (authored pattern geometry, not a stated flex-eligible dial).

modeling_assumptions.basis: Real, well-known cutting-room concern: a one-way-directional or napped print can force extra yardage on a fold-cut layout.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing on the Twist only -- see FACILITATOR.md.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: Devon's shop chalk-marks each layout by hand with tailor's chalk and cuts with scissors or a hand-held rotary cutter -- not an automated, computerized (CNC-style) fabric-cutting machine.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Real, general cutting-room knowledge: small custom-apparel shops typically run on manual marking and cutting; automated cutters are a large-factory, high-volume investment. Consistent with Rotary cutter -- Wikipedia (Appendix G) on the tool's real use in garment cutting.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Narrative/context only -- does not change any figure in Appendix A-D. Explains why Cut Open's marking time exceeds Cut on the Fold's (more pieces traced/matched by hand), already captured numerically in Appendix C.

catalog.ask: Devon has 90 minutes before the cutting room needs an answer: a rush order of 40 aprons, and two ways to lay the pattern out on the bolt. One layout uses less fabric. The other takes less time to mark and cut. Everyone assumes "less fabric" means "cheaper" -- do the math before you bet the order on it.
